# Load required packages and custom settings

```{r}
# Check if 'pacman' is installed; if not, install it
# 'pacman' helps manage and load R packages efficiently
if (!require(pacman)) {
  install.packages("pacman")
}

# Load required packages using pacman
pacman::p_load(
  vroom,        # Fast reading of large csv files
  tidyverse,    # Data wrangling and visualization
  binom,        # Binomial confidence intervals
  glue,         # String interpolation
  here,         # Relative file paths
  patchwork,    # Combine ggplots
  modelsummary, # Summarizing model outputs
  tinytable,    # Lightweight table creation for reports
  arrow,        # Apache Parquet support
  DiagrammeR,   # Diagram creation and visualization
  DiagrammeRsvg, # SVG export for diagrams
  rsvg          # Convert SVG to other formats
)

# Load a GitHub package for additional functionality
devtools::install_github("graemeblair/stdidx")
library(stdidx)

# Load tidylog for logging data manipulation transparently
library("tidylog", warn.conflicts = FALSE)

# Load custom plotting theme and utility functions
options(es.use_symbols = TRUE) # Use symbols in plots
source(here("functions", "utils.r")) # Custom utility functions
ggplot2::theme_set(custom_theme())   # Apply custom ggplot theme
```

# Create a diagram to visualize data pipeline

## Figure 1

```{r}
################################################################################
# FIGURE 1
# This figure illustrates the data processing pipeline, showing the flow 
# from raw data sources to final datasets. It helps readers understand
# the logical steps involved in dataset generation.
################################################################################

# Define a data pipeline using DiagrammeR
graph <- grViz("
digraph civic_pipeline {
  graph [rankdir = TB, layout = dot]
  node [shape = box, style = filled, fontname = Helvetica, fontsize = 12]

  // Raw Data Sources
  IRS       [label = 'IRS Master Business File', fillcolor = lightblue]
  filings   [label = 'Digitized 990 Filings', fillcolor = lightblue]
  urls      [label = 'Organizational URLs', fillcolor = lightblue]
  about     [label = 'Organizational About Pages', fillcolor = lightblue]

  // Data Extraction
  search      [label = 'Find URLs via Bing Search API', fillcolor = white]
  scrape      [label = 'Extract Website Texts', fillcolor = white]
  extractXML  [label = 'Extract XMLs', fillcolor = white]
  extractGeo  [label = 'Extract Geolocations', fillcolor = white]

  // Derived Datasets
  corpus    [label = 'Descriptive Text Corpus', fillcolor = palegreen]
  geolocate [label = 'Geolocations', fillcolor = palegreen]
  activities [label = 'Organizational Activities', fillcolor = palegreen]

  // Data Transformation
  nlp       [label = 'Rule-based Classification (NLP)', fillcolor = gainsboro]
  ml        [label = 'Supervised Classification (ML)', fillcolor = gainsboro]

  // Final Datasets
  classification [label = 'Organizational Classification', fillcolor = khaki]
  dataset   [label = 'Civic Opportunity Datasets', fillcolor = khaki]

  // Main Flow Edges
  IRS -> filings
  IRS -> search
  search -> urls
  urls -> about
  about -> scrape
  scrape -> corpus
  filings -> extractXML
  extractXML -> corpus
  urls -> extractGeo
  extractGeo -> geolocate
  IRS -> extractGeo
  corpus -> nlp
  corpus -> ml
  nlp -> activities
  ml -> classification
  activities -> dataset
  geolocate -> dataset
  geolocate -> classification

  // Invisible anchor to pull legend to top right
  anchor [style=invis, width=0, height=0]

  // Legend cluster (fully internal)
  subgraph cluster_legend {
    label = 'Type'
    fontsize = 12
    style = dashed
    color = gray

    legend1 [label = 'Raw Data Sources', fillcolor = lightblue, style = filled, shape = box]
    legend2 [label = 'Derived Datasets', fillcolor = palegreen, style = filled, shape = box]
    legend3 [label = 'Final Datasets', fillcolor = khaki, style = filled, shape = box]
    legend4 [label = 'Data Extraction', fillcolor = white, style = filled, shape = box]
    legend5 [label = 'Data Transformation', fillcolor = gainsboro, style = filled, shape = box]

    legend1 -> legend2 [style=invis]
    legend2 -> legend3 [style=invis]
    legend3 -> legend4 [style=invis]
    legend4 -> legend5 [style=invis]
    anchor -> legend1 [style=invis]
  }
}
")

# Convert diagram to SVG and PNG formats for publication
svg <- export_svg(graph) # Export as SVG
charToRaw(svg) %>% rsvg_png(here("plots", "figure1.png")) # Convert to PNG
```

# Load and preprocess data

```{r}
# Load organizational data from raw IRS tax records and websites
ind_org_df <- vroom::vroom(here("raw_data", "ind_org_df.csv")) 

# Export the file to parquet   
# ?????? Note: This may exceed GitHub’s file size limit???exclude from version control
arrow::write_parquet(ind_org_df, here("raw_data", "ind_org_df.parquet"))

# Export the file to RDS 
# ?????? Note: This may exceed GitHub’s file size limit???exclude from version control
readr::write_rds(ind_org_df, here("raw_data", "ind_org_df.rds"))

# Display the number of organizations in the dataset
nrow(ind_org_df) # 1.8M

# Show the column names of the dataset
names(ind_org_df) # 17 variables 
```

```{r}
# Load SDOH (Social Determinants of Health) data from CDC, aggregated by county and ZIP code

# County-level data
sdoh_county <- read_csv(here("raw_data", "sdoh_county.csv")) %>%
  select(StateAbbr, StateDesc, LocationID, MeasureID, Data_Value, TotalPopulation, Geolocation)

# Reshape county data from long to wide format
sdoh_county_wide <- sdoh_county %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = MeasureID, values_from = Data_Value)

# ZIP code-level data
sdoh_zcta <- read_csv(here("raw_data", "sdoh_zcta.csv")) %>%
  select(LocationID, MeasureID, Data_Value, TotalPopulation, Geolocation)

# Reshape ZIP code data from long to wide format
sdoh_zcta_wide <- sdoh_zcta %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = MeasureID, values_from = Data_Value)
```

# Data checks

```{r}
# Display the size of the dataset
nrow(ind_org_df) # ~1.3M organizations

# Check the proportion of organizations using P.O. boxes
mean(ind_org_df$is_po) # ~23% use P.O. boxes
```

```{r}
# Compare predictions: all orgs vs. non???P.O. Box orgs

# Generate predicted category distribution with CIs for all orgs
df_all <- get_predicted_percent_ci(ind_org_df, "All organizations")

# Generate the same for non???P.O. Box organizations
df_box <- get_predicted_percent_ci(ind_org_df %>% filter(is_po != 1), "Excluding P.O. Box")

# Combine both summaries into a single dataframe for plotting/comparison
comparison_df <- bind_rows(df_all, df_box)

# Spread the comparison data to wide format for easy comparison
comparison_wide <- comparison_df %>%
  select(group, predicted, percent) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = percent)

# Add a column for percent difference
comparison_wide <- comparison_wide %>%
  mutate(
    percent_diff = (`Excluding P.O. Box` - `All organizations`),
    percent_diff_abs = abs(percent_diff)
  )

# View results sorted by largest absolute difference
percent_diff <- comparison_wide %>%
  arrange(desc(percent_diff_abs)) %>%
  select(predicted, `All organizations`, `Excluding P.O. Box`, percent_diff) %>%
  pull(percent_diff)

mean(abs(percent_diff)) # ~0.09
sd(abs(percent_diff)) # ~0.10

comparison_wide
```

### Table S2

```{r}
################################################################################
# Table s2
################################################################################

# Create a cleaner version of the comparison table
table_s2 <- comparison_wide %>%
  mutate(
    `Difference (%)` = round(percent_diff, 2),
    `All organizations` = round(`All organizations`, 2),
    `Excluding P.O. Box` = round(`Excluding P.O. Box`, 2)
  ) %>%
  select(
    `Organizational Type` = predicted,
    `All organizations`,
    `Excluding P.O. Box`,
    `Difference (%)`
  )

# Note: Percentages are rounded to two decimal places. Difference is calculated as the percentage in the non???P.O. Box sample minus the full sample

datasummary_df(
  table_s2,
  output = "latex",
  fmt = 2,
  title = "Table S2: Comparison of Organizational Types With and Without P.O. Box Exclusion"
) %>%
  save_tt(
    here("tables", "tables2.tex"),
    overwrite = TRUE
  )
```

```{r}
# Compare predicted category shares across all orgs and orgs without P.O. Boxes
# Produce a side-by-side comparison of predicted categories with or without P.O. Boxes
left_join(
  ind_org_df %>%
    filter(!is.na(predicted)) %>%
    count(predicted) %>%
    mutate(percent = n / sum(n) * 100) %>%
    select(predicted, percent),
  ind_org_df %>%
    filter(is_po != 1, !is.na(predicted)) %>%
    count(predicted) %>%
    mutate(without_po_percent = n / sum(n) * 100) %>%
    select(predicted, without_po_percent)
)
```

```{r}
# Remove P.O. Box???only organizations from the dataset
ind_org_df <- ind_org_df %>%
  filter(is_po != 1)

# Check the number of organizations after filtering
nrow(ind_org_df) # 1,363,701
```
  
# Create datasets

```{r}
# Create two new variables:
# opp_binary: 1 if the org offers any civic opportunity
# opp_mean: average of the four opportunity indicators
# Note: These fields already exist in the dataset ??? this step is for reproducibility.
# The function idx_mean() computes the row-wise mean across the four binary indicators.

ind_org_df <- ind_org_df %>%
  mutate(
    opp_binary = ifelse(volunteer == 1 | membership == 1 | take_action == 1 | events == 1, 1, 0),
    opp_mean = idx_mean(volunteer, membership, take_action, events)
  )

# Subset to organizations that offer at least one civic opportunity
civic_orgs <- ind_org_df %>%
  filter(opp_binary == 1)
```

## The second datasets (what organizations do)

### County 

```{r}
# First, group by FIPS (county), internal grouping_value (e.g., chapters), and state
cnts_counts <- ind_org_df %>%
  group_by(FIPS, grouping_value, state) %>%
  summarise(
    b = max(opp_binary, na.rm = TRUE),          # Whether any org in the group offers civic opportunity
    m = max(opp_mean, na.rm = TRUE),            # Max of average opportunity score in the group
    volunteer_m = max(volunteer, na.rm = TRUE), # Max value for each indicator within the group
    membership_m = max(membership, na.rm = TRUE),
    take_action_m = max(take_action, na.rm = TRUE),
    events_m = max(events, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  group_by(FIPS, state) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),                                      # Number of organizational groupings in the county
    civic_org_sum = sum(b),                      # Total number of groups with civic opportunity
    civic_opp_sum = sum(m),                      # Sum of opportunity scores across groups
    volunteer_sum = sum(volunteer_m),
    membership_sum = sum(membership_m),
    take_action_sum = sum(take_action_m),
    events_sum = sum(events_m)
  )

# Calculate the share of counties with orgs but no civic opportunity
(cnts_counts %>%
  filter(n != 0, civic_org_sum == 0) %>%
  nrow()) / (nrow(cnts_counts)) # About 3% = civic deserts
```

```{r}
# Join civic opportunity summaries with SDOH county-level data
cnts_counts_cov <- cnts_counts %>%
  left_join(
    sdoh_county_wide %>%
      select(-StateDesc),  # Remove verbose label column
    by = c(
      "FIPS" = "LocationID",  # Match on county FIPS code
      "state" = "StateAbbr"   # Match on state abbreviation
    )
  )

# Normalize counts by population and create derived indicators (e.g., quintiles)
cnts_counts_cov <- cnts_counts_cov %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    civic_org_sum_normalized = 100000 * civic_org_sum / TotalPopulation,         # Orgs per 100k
    civic_opp_sum_normalized = 100000 * civic_opp_sum / TotalPopulation,         # Opportunities per 100k
    civic_opp_index = dplyr::ntile(civic_opp_sum_normalized, 5),                 # Quintile index (1???5)
    volunteer_sum_normalized = 100000 * volunteer_sum / TotalPopulation,
    membership_sum_normalized = 100000 * membership_sum / TotalPopulation,
    take_action_sum_normalized = 100000 * take_action_sum / TotalPopulation,
    events_sum_normalized = 100000 * events_sum / TotalPopulation
  )

# Sanity check: Are there any counties with no orgs or no civic opps?
round(mean(cnts_counts$n == 0), 2)            # Should be 0 ??? all counties have orgs
round(mean(cnts_counts$civic_opp_sum == 0), 2) # Should be ~0.03 ??? civic deserts

# Drop specific SDOH indicators if not needed for analysis
cnts_counts_cov <- cnts_counts_cov %>%
  select(-c("HCOST", "CROWD", "AGE65"))

# Check SDOH coverage gaps ??? how many counties missing CDC data?
length(setdiff(cnts_counts$FIPS, sdoh_county_wide$LocationID))  # ~78 counties
78 / 3281  # ~2% of counties missing ??? consistent with CDC suppression
```

```{r}
# Save cleaned and merged county-level dataset to CSV
write_csv(
  cnts_counts_cov %>% select(-matches("Geo")),  # Remove geolocation columns before export
  here("data_outputs", "cnty_counts_cov.csv")
)

# Save the same dataset in RDS format for fast reloading in R
write_rds(  # Note: Should be `write_rds()` here
  cnts_counts_cov %>% select(-matches("Geo")),
  here("data_outputs", "cnty_counts_cov.rds")
)
```

### ZIP code

```{r}
# Summarize civic opportunity data by ZIP Code Tabulation Area (ZCTA), grouping_value, and state
zcta_counts <- ind_org_df %>%
  group_by(ZCTA, grouping_value, state) %>%
  summarise(
    m = max(opp_mean, na.rm = TRUE),             # Max average civic opportunity score
    b = max(opp_binary, na.rm = TRUE),           # Binary: any civic opportunity present
    volunteer_m = max(volunteer, na.rm = TRUE),  # Max of individual indicators
    membership_m = max(membership, na.rm = TRUE),
    take_action_m = max(take_action, na.rm = TRUE),
    events_m = max(events, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  group_by(ZCTA, state) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),                                      # Number of organizational groupings
    civic_org_sum = sum(b),                      # Number offering any civic opportunity
    civic_opp_sum = sum(m),                      # Total opportunity score
    volunteer_sum = sum(volunteer_m),
    membership_sum = sum(membership_m),
    take_action_sum = sum(take_action_m),
    events_sum = sum(events_m)
  )

# Calculate what proportion of ZIPs are civic deserts
(zcta_counts %>%
  filter(n != 0, civic_org_sum == 0) %>%
  nrow()) / (nrow(zcta_counts))  # ~17% of ZIP codes are civic deserts
```

```{r}
# Join ZIP-level civic summaries with SDOH covariates from the CDC
zcta_counts_cov <- zcta_counts %>%
  left_join(sdoh_zcta_wide, by = c("ZCTA" = "LocationID")) %>%
  ungroup()

# Create population-normalized metrics and a civic opportunity quintile index
zcta_counts_cov <- zcta_counts_cov %>%
  mutate(
    civic_org_sum_normalized = 100000 * civic_org_sum / TotalPopulation,          # Orgs per 100k people
    civic_opp_sum_normalized = 100000 * civic_opp_sum / TotalPopulation,          # Opps per 100k
    civic_opp_index = ntile(civic_opp_sum_normalized, 5),                          # Quintile index (1???5)
    volunteer_sum_normalized = 100000 * volunteer_sum / TotalPopulation,
    membership_sum_normalized = 100000 * membership_sum / TotalPopulation,
    take_action_sum_normalized = 100000 * take_action_sum / TotalPopulation,
    events_sum_normalized = 100000 * events_sum / TotalPopulation
  ) %>%
  select(-c("HCOST", "CROWD", "AGE65"))  # Drop unneeded SDOH columns for simplicity

# Check ZIPs with no SDOH match ??? may reflect suppressed or rural areas
length(setdiff(zcta_counts$ZCTA, sdoh_zcta_wide$LocationID))  # 2,980 ZIPs not matched
2980 / 30988  # ~10% of ZIPs are missing from SDOH data
```

```{r}
# Save ZIP-level dataset to CSV, excluding geolocation fields
write_csv(
  zcta_counts_cov %>% select(-Geolocation),
  here("data_outputs", "zcta_counts_cov.csv")
)

# Save the same data in RDS format for efficient R loading
write_rds(
  zcta_counts_cov %>% select(-Geolocation),
  here("data_outputs", "zcta_counts_cov.rds")
)
```

## The third datasets (what organizations are)

```{r}
# Define vector of predicted class labels (model outputs)
class_vec <- c(
  "arts", "civic", "community", "econ", "education", "foundation",
  "health", "hobby", "housing", "professional", "religious",
  "research", "socialfraternal", "unions", "youth"
)

# Recode predicted categories into human-readable class labels
# These will be used in summary tables and visualizations
civic_orgs <- civic_orgs %>%
  mutate(class = case_match(
    predicted,
    class_vec[1] ~ "Arts & Cultural",
    class_vec[2] ~ "Political",
    class_vec[3] ~ "Community",
    class_vec[4] ~ "Economic",
    class_vec[5] ~ "Education",
    class_vec[6] ~ "Foundations",
    class_vec[7] ~ "Healthcare",
    class_vec[8] ~ "Hobby & Sports",
    class_vec[9] ~ "Housing",
    class_vec[10] ~ "Professional",
    class_vec[11] ~ "Religious",
    class_vec[12] ~ "Research & Think Tank",
    class_vec[13] ~ "Social & Fraternal",
    class_vec[14] ~ "Unions",
    class_vec[15] ~ "Youth"
  ))
```

### County

```{r}
# Group civic orgs by county and class, and count how many fall into each category
cnty_civic_org_type <- civic_orgs %>%
  group_by(FIPS, class) %>%
  count() %>%                 # Count number of orgs in each class per county
  ungroup()

# Compute share of each class within each county and identify the most common category
cnty_civic_org_type <- cnty_civic_org_type %>%
  group_by(FIPS) %>%
  mutate(freq = n / sum(n)) %>%                          # Proportion of each class
  mutate(primary_org_cat = class[which.max(freq)]) %>%   # Class with the highest share
  ungroup()

# Save county-level org type distribution
write_csv(cnty_civic_org_type, here("data_outputs", "cnty_civic_org_type.csv"))
write_rds(cnty_civic_org_type, here("data_outputs", "cnty_civic_org_type.rds"))
```

#### Dashboard 

```{r}
# Count number of civic orgs by county (FIPS), state, and class
cnty_civic_org_type_dashboard <- civic_orgs %>%
  group_by(state, FIPS, class) %>%
  count() %>%
  ungroup()

# For each county, compute frequency of each class and assign the dominant category
cnty_civic_org_type_dashboard <- cnty_civic_org_type_dashboard %>%
  group_by(FIPS) %>%
  mutate(freq = n / sum(n)) %>%                          # Share of each org class in county
  mutate(primary_org_cat = class[which.max(freq)]) %>%   # Dominant class
  ungroup()

# Merge with SDOH data to include population
cnty_civic_type_dashboard <- cnty_civic_org_type_dashboard %>%
  left_join(
    sdoh_county_wide %>%
      select(-StateDesc),                                # Drop verbose state name
    by = c("FIPS" = "LocationID", "state" = "StateAbbr")
  )

# Final formatting: keep selected columns and compute normalized count per 100,000
cnty_civic_type_dashboard <- cnty_civic_type_dashboard %>%
  select(state, FIPS, class, n, freq, primary_org_cat, TotalPopulation) %>%
  mutate(normalized_n = n / TotalPopulation) %>%         # Count per capita
  select(state, FIPS, class, n, normalized_n, freq, primary_org_cat, TotalPopulation)


# Export final dashboard-ready dataset as CSV
write_csv(cnty_civic_type_dashboard, here("data_outputs", "cnty_civic_type_dashboard.csv"))
```

### ZIP code 

```{r}
# Group civic organizations by ZIP code and class, then count frequency
zcta_civic_org_type <- civic_orgs %>%
  group_by(ZCTA, class) %>%
  count() %>%
  ungroup()

# Within each ZIP code, calculate class proportions and identify the dominant category
zcta_civic_org_type <- zcta_civic_org_type %>%
  group_by(ZCTA) %>%
  mutate(freq = n / sum(n)) %>%                          # Class share in ZIP
  mutate(primary_org_cat = class[which.max(freq)]) %>%   # Most frequent class
  ungroup()

# Save the ZIP-level classification summary as CSV and RDS
write_csv(zcta_civic_org_type, here("data_outputs", "zcta_civic_org_type.csv"))
write_rds(zcta_civic_org_type, here("data_outputs", "zcta_civic_org_type.rds"))
```
